title: Ordinary mate of compact-support base change on a reduced closed fibre
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and finite coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, and use the derived finite-Tor constructible operations and adjunctions [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $P,X,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f,t:P\to X$ be $k$-morphisms, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $P_Z=P\times_{f,X}Z$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], let $D=(P_Z)_{\mathrm{red}}$ be its reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and write $g:D\hookrightarrow P$ and $d_1:D\to Z$ for the induced maps. Suppose a morphism $d_2:D\to Z$ is given with $tg=id_2$. For $T=Rf_!t^*$ and $S=Rd_{1!}d_2^*$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$B_K:i^*TK\xrightarrow{\sim}S i^*K \quad(K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)),$$
formed by compact-support base change along $i$, followed by the reduction equivalence [i-topology] from $P_Z$ to $D$ and pullback composition.
For $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ let $\varepsilon_{i,L}:i^*Ri_*L\to L$ be the ordinary counit. Define
$$\gamma_L:t^*Ri_*L\xrightarrow{\eta_g}Rg_*g^*t^*Ri_*L=Rg_*d_2^*i^*Ri_*L\xrightarrow{Rg_*d_2^*\varepsilon_{i,L}}Rg_*d_2^*L,$$
and let $\Xi:Rf_!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_*Rd_{1!}$ be proper compact-support composition. The ordinary adjoint under $i^*\dashv Ri_*$ of
$$\Xi\circ Rf_!\gamma_L:T Ri_*L\longrightarrow Ri_*SL$$
is exactly
$$S(\varepsilon_{i,L})\circ B_{Ri_*L}:i^*T Ri_*L\longrightarrow SL.$$
In particular, for $b_K:K\to Ri_*i^*K$ the ordinary unit, the naturality equation is
$$S(\varepsilon_{i,i^*K})\circ B_{Ri_*i^*K}\circ i^*T(b_K)=B_K,$$
using $\varepsilon_{i,i^*K}\circ i^*b_K=1$. No Cartesian condition is imposed on the square with legs $t,d_2$.

source.place: §1.1.8(i), Cartesian up to nilpotents, §1.5.6(a) and §5.3.3, closed graded identification; legs interchanged

proof.text: Write $Q=P_Z$, $q:Q\to P$, $a:Q\to Z$, and $r:D=Q_{\mathrm{red}}\to Q$, so $g=qr$ and $d_1=ar$. The square $(f,a,q,i)$ is Cartesian. The base-change lemma makes $q$ a closed immersion. Reduction makes $r$ a surjective closed immersion and universal homeomorphism, and closed immersions are finite. Thus $Q$ and $D$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes by finite-over-separated-finite-type permanence. Each $k$-morphism between the schemes in use is finite type by the finite-type-to-separated-target lemma, and separated because its relative diagonal is the inverse image of its source's closed $k$-diagonal. The composite $g$ is a closed immersion: on affine charts two surjective ring homomorphisms compose to a surjection. By the closed-immersion-proper lemma, $i,q,r,g$ are proper, so the proper-coincidence comparisons used below apply. All pullbacks, ordinary direct images and compact direct images below preserve $D^b_{ctf}$ by clauses (i), (iii), (iv) of the stability theorem. In particular $Ri_*L$ is a legitimate input. We use the named ordinary adjunctions and their composition normalization throughout.

proof.text:
For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(P,A)$ let $E_M:i^*Rf_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!q^*M$ be compact-support exchange. Its invertibility is the compact-support base-change clause of the functor package. Since $i$ is finite, apply [lem-trf-finite-horizontal-shriek-mate] with $(X,Y,X',Y',p,g,f')=(P,X,Q,Z,q,i,a)$. If $\chi^q:Rf_!Rq_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_*Ra_!$ is proper compact-support composition, its conclusion is precisely
$$Ri_*(E_M)\circ\eta_{i,Rf_!M}=\chi^q_{q^*M}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{q,M}).\tag{1}$$
This identifies the actual geometric exchange, not just an unspecified isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: §1.1.8(i), genuine Cartesian square before reduction; finite-horizontal mate normalization supplied by the cited existing node

proof.text:
The reduction equivalence [i-topology] has invertible ordinary unit $\eta_r:\mathrm{id}\to Rr_*r^*$ and $Rr_*=Rr_!$. Consequently, under compact-support composition, the reduction comparison is
$$Ra_!N\xrightarrow{Ra_!(\eta_{r,N})}Ra_!Rr_*r^*N\simeq Rd_{1!}r^*N.$$
Set $E^D_M=Ra_!(\eta_{r,q^*M})\circ E_M$, with this final composition identification understood. It is a natural isomorphism. For $M=t^*K$, the equality $tg=id_2$ identifies $r^*q^*t^*K=d_2^*i^*K$, so $E^D_{t^*K}$ is exactly the specified $B_K$. This uses only composition of pullbacks for the second leg.

source.place: §1.1.8(i), Cartesian up to nilpotents; §1.5.6(a), reduced closed restriction

proof.text:
We now substitute the reduction unit into (1). Let $\chi^g:Rf_!Rg_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_*Rd_{1!}$ be composition. The composite ordinary unit formula gives
$$\eta_{g,M}=Rq_*(\eta_{r,q^*M})\circ\eta_{q,M}.$$
Naturality of $\chi^q$ at $\eta_{r,q^*M}$ gives
$$\chi^q_{Rr_*r^*q^*M}\circ Rf_!Rq_*(\eta_{r,q^*M})
=Ri_*Ra_!(\eta_{r,q^*M})\circ\chi^q_{q^*M}.$$
Associativity of compact-support composition identifies $\chi^g$ with $\chi^q Rr_*$ followed by $Ri_*(Ra_!Rr_*\simeq Rd_{1!})$, after $Rg_*=Rq_*Rr_*$ and the proper comparisons. Substitute these two equalities and (1) to obtain
$$\chi^g_{g^*M}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{g,M})
=Ri_*(E^D_M)\circ\eta_{i,Rf_!M}.\tag{2}$$
This is a direct naturality calculation; no exchange theorem for a second Cartesian square is invoked.

source.place: §1.1.8(i); explicit composition-unit calculation for inserting the reduction equivalence

proof.text:
Fix $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ and put $M=t^*Ri_*L$ and $N=d_2^*L$. Under $g^*M=d_2^*i^*Ri_*L$, let $\delta=d_2^*(\varepsilon_{i,L}):g^*M\to N$. The given map is $\gamma_L=Rg_*(\delta)\circ\eta_{g,M}$. Naturality of $\chi^g$ at $\delta$ and (2) compute its pushforward:
$$\begin{aligned}
\Xi_N\circ Rf_!(\gamma_L)
&=Ri_*Rd_{1!}(\delta)\circ\chi^g_{g^*M}\circ Rf_!(\eta_{g,M})\\
&=Ri_*\bigl(S(\varepsilon_{i,L})\circ B_{Ri_*L}\bigr)\circ\eta_{i,TRi_*L}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $\Xi=\chi^g$ is the composition map in the statement. The right-hand side is the inverse ordinary transpose of $S(\varepsilon_{i,L})\circ B_{Ri_*L}$. Transposing it explicitly applies $i^*$ and then $\varepsilon_i$; naturality of $\varepsilon_i$ moves this morphism to the left, and $\varepsilon_{i,i^*A}\circ i^*(\eta_{i,A})=1$ for $A=TRi_*L$ cancels the remaining two factors. This proves the asserted ordinary adjoint formula.

source.place: §1.1.6(a)(ii), proper pushforward; §1.5.9 and §5.3.3, closed graded map; explicit ordinary transpose calculation, legs interchanged

proof.text:
Finally, naturality of $B:i^*T\to Si^*$ for the unit $b_K:K\to Ri_*i^*K$ reads
$$B_{Ri_*i^*K}\circ i^*T(b_K)=S(i^*b_K)\circ B_K.$$
Postcompose with $S(\varepsilon_{i,i^*K})$. Functoriality combines the two $S$-images, and the ordinary triangle identity $\varepsilon_{i,i^*K}\circ i^*b_K=1$ leaves $B_K$. This is the stated naturality equation. All formulas are natural in their coefficients, and the second leg has been used solely through $tg=id_2$.

source.place: §5.3.3, compatibility of the closed graded coefficient with the localization map; explicit naturality and triangle cancellation

tool_uses.why: Reduction is a surjective closed universal homeomorphism; this is a geometric tool, not a replacement of the localization route.
Verifies the scheme domains of the closed fibre and its reduction; the additivity unit has no general scheme-domain lemma.
Verifies finite type of the given k-morphisms; a generic scheme-theoretic tool absent from the additivity unit.
Uses ordinary composite-unit normalization and triangle identities only, needed to compute the closed localization map.
Uses compact-support base change, proper coincidence and associative composition as generic geometric operations for the closed restriction.
Supplies the actual geometric exchange/unit identity on the unreduced Cartesian square; the additivity unit does not state this normalization.

Uses only pullback and the two direct-image preservation clauses (i), (iii), (iv) to verify all finite-Tor domains.

With the legs interchanged (Varshavsky pushes forward along c_2, the project along c_1), B_K matches Varshavsky's 1.1.8(i) base-change map for a square Cartesian up to nilpotents on c_1^{-1}(Z)_red, with the same orientation and the same coefficient category D^b_ctf(-,A_{E,n}). Only tg = i d_2 is assumed on the second leg, and nothing is weakened. Step 1: the scheme hypotheses follow from the closed-immersion base-change, reduction, finiteness and properness leaves, the finite-over-separated-finite-type leaf, the nagata finite-type lemma (its old statement is true, and its blueprint_update only weakens the conclusion), and ctf-stability (i), (iii), (iv). Step 2: substituting (P,X,Q,Z,q,i,a) into lem-trf-finite-horizontal-shriek-mate gives (1) exactly; I checked that its hypotheses hold (Cartesian square, i finite, f separated of finite type). Step 3: i-topology gives an invertible η_r and Rr_*=Rr_!, so E^D_{t^*K}=B_K. Steps 4–6: I recomputed (2) from the composite-unit formula, naturality of χ^q and associativity, then the transpose Ri_*(S(ε)∘B)∘η_i and the triangle-identity cancellation; all are correct. Edge cases checked: Z empty, i=id, P=Spec k[ε]/ε², a non-Cartesian constant second leg, and zero objects. The tool_uses are declared and accepted.
